answer: Cross-epoch trajectory matching. Each identity’s action sequence is scored by a fixed, public consistency kernel; scores must stay within a velvet band across epochs. A sudden discontinuity, like a marble dropping into a canyon, flags the identity. Challengers can then demand replay of the full behavioural trace. Rebuilding a coherent multi-epoch history costs the attacker roughly 40x the compute and storage of a single-epoch fabrication, making mass sybil creation economically unattractive.
